evidence.s1_requirements: Every point of steps/1.md is met. `snapshot()` returns `{version, root}` as a plain object (src/BehaviourTree.ts:133). `BehaviourTreeSnapshot` and `NodeSnapshot` are exported (step1.patch src/index.ts). `restore()` checks the whole snapshot first, then applies it (BehaviourTree.ts:143-168). Node state, children, repeat and retry current and target counts, the lotto pick (`selectedChild` index) and wait total and waited durations are all saved. A restored wait sets `initialUpdateTime = now - waitedDuration` (Wait.ts:146), so time between snapshot and restore is not counted in either time mode. Finished trees restore as finished; on the next step they reset and pick again because Repeat, Lotto and Wait re-pick on READY. The README has an API section with an example. The version went from 4.3.1 to 4.4.0 with a Version History row.
evidence.s1_correctness: Each node class stores what it needs: Lotto, Repeat, Retry, Wait, and Action (a settled promise result). Node ids are restored, so `getTreeNodeDetails()` matches the original. Every composite and decorator updates a child that is READY or RUNNING (Sequence.ts:30, Flip.ts:28, etc.), so restored states continue correctly. A new `updatePromise` field (Action.ts:72, 138, 150) stops a promise from before the restore from changing the node. Edge cases are handled: a lotto aborted by its guard before picking (null `selectedChild` allowed unless RUNNING), an infinite delta time (clamped to MAX_VALUE), and the clock going backwards. A rejected promise rebuilds the same error text via `String(value)`. Tests compare the original and restored trees step by step for sequence, selector, parallel, race, all, flip, succeed, fail, nested repeat, retry and branch, plus a guard-abort case.
evidence.s2_validation: A definition fingerprint (`canonicalise` plus a cyrb53 hash, src/DefinitionFingerprint.ts) fills in the defaults the MDSL converter adds (`args: []`, `succeedOnAbort`). A detailed MDSL/JSON pair is tested both ways (step2.patch test 977-1006). A different definition is rejected with 'invalid snapshot: the snapshot does not match the tree's definition' (BehaviourTree.ts:158), including when only an action argument, guard, callback or lotto weight differs. null, undefined, strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, `{}` and partial snapshots are rejected; each test checks the tree is unchanged afterwards (test 1127-1154). A pending promise is saved as READY through `getSnapshotState` (Action.ts:205), tested (entry callback runs again), and documented in the README. Weaknesses: global subtrees registered with `BehaviourTree.register` are not part of the fingerprint, because only the tree's own `json` is hashed (BehaviourTree.ts:69). The test 'a guard abort state' uses `until(Done, true)`, which changes an argument, not the abort state; the MDSL syntax for that is `then succeed` (MDSLNodeAttributeParser.ts:71).
evidence.s3_fixes: Step 3 changes only test/Snapshot.spec.ts (step3.patch) and makes one test commit (787b281). This fits the code: `applySnapshot` sets `_state` directly without `setState` (Node.ts:350), so `onNodeStateChange` is never called during restore, and the promise result is copied (Action.ts:255, done in 80dc8db), so a snapshot does not share objects with the tree. The new tests cover several step counts, restoring into a tree already stepped, the transitions of the next step, independence after stepping the original and the restored tree, and equality of a snapshot taken right after restore. Remaining gap: for a RUNNING wait in clock mode, `getOwnSnapshot` computes `now - initialUpdateTime` (Wait.ts:115-117). With a real clock, a snapshot taken right after `restore(s)` can differ from `s` by the milliseconds that passed. The tests use fake timers, so they cannot catch this.
evidence.design: Each node type owns its state through `getOwnSnapshot`, `validateOwnSnapshot` and `applyOwnSnapshot` overrides (Node.ts:364-382), and the public API is two typed methods with the snapshot types exported. Small validation helpers live in src/SnapshotValidation.ts. Drawbacks: a new protected `getChildNodes()` duplicates the existing `getChildren` on Composite and Decorator. The `getOwnSnapshot(): object` methods and the `as NodeSnapshot`/`as RepeatNodeSnapshot` casts lose the discriminated-union typing. `uid` is no longer readonly. The rest follows the repository's JSDoc and naming style.
evidence.tests: A single new file, test/Snapshot.spec.ts, uses mocha, chai and sinon fake timers in line with the repository. It has a helper that steps the original and restored trees side by side and compares node details and the call log after each step, which tests the 'behaves exactly as' requirement meaningfully. It covers every composite and decorator, both wait time modes, random choices, finished trees, settled and pending promises, invalid input, definition matching and the step 3 reports. No existing test was removed or weakened; step 2 changed only the agent's own step 1 tests so the node-level checks are still reached. Flaws: the mislabeled 'guard abort state' case; `stepMore` swallows all errors (step3.patch:131-135); the first step 3 test only asserts `previousState !== state`.
evidence.docs: The README adds snapshot() and restore(snapshot) entries and a 'Saving and Restoring a Tree' section. Its example is correct: agent functions are called with `this` bound to the agent (Lookup.ts:75), and the restored tree resumes at WaitForApproval. The section says what is kept, how finished trees behave, the restore checks, and the pending-promise limitation (step2.patch README 28). The Version History has a 4.4.0 row with sub-rows, and package.json and package-lock.json are bumped to 4.4.0, following the repository's convention.
evidence.process: The commits are focused and follow conventional-commit style (feat, fix, docs, chore, build, test), and the messages match the changes. dist is rebuilt in separate commits, consistent with dist being tracked. No new dependencies and no unrequested public features. Minor: commit b4fe76c 'docs: spec for tree snapshot and restore' adds a file that is not in the final tree. Step 1 has some combined commits, such as 2b4fb73, which does validation and cross-node tests together. Step 3's commit does not record why no source fix was needed.

unmet_requirements: Step 3 report 2 (partly): with the real clock, a snapshot taken right after restore(s) of a running wait node can differ from s by the milliseconds since the restore (Wait.ts:115-117); this is only tested with fake timers

Step 2 (edge): the definition fingerprint ignores global subtrees registered with BehaviourTree.register, so a snapshot can be accepted by a tree whose registered subtree differs only in arguments or attributes
strengths: Each node class saves and restores its own state, and the whole snapshot is checked before anything is applied, so a rejected restore leaves the tree untouched and restore never calls `setState` or agent functions

Tests compare the original and restored trees step by step across every node type and many snapshot points, plus focused edge cases (both wait time modes, a lotto aborted by its guard, promises, invalid input, MDSL/JSON equivalence)
README section with a correct example, the pending-promise limitation, and the version bump and Version History row in the repository's format
issues: A running clock-mode wait computes its waited time when `snapshot()` is called, so a snapshot taken right after `restore(s)` may not equal `s` with a real clock; the step 3 equality tests depend on fake timers
The definition fingerprint covers only the tree's own definition, not globally registered subtrees, and the test named 'a guard abort state' changes a guard argument instead of the abort state
Type safety is weakened by `getOwnSnapshot(): object` and casts, and the new `getChildNodes()` duplicates the existing `getChildren`; in step 3 the `stepMore` helper swallows all errors
review.verdict: This is a well-structured, thoroughly tested snapshot and restore feature: definitions are checked by fingerprint, pending promises are handled as asked, and the README is complete. I would merge it after small follow-ups: freeze the clock-mode waited time until the next update so a snapshot right after restore equals the input, and include registered subtrees in the fingerprint or document that they are not.
